new_statements.rule_in_words: For Sea Dayak (Iban) of the Batang Lupar tribes, Balau explicitly included: most words are disyllabic and the accent generally falls on the first (= penultimate) syllable; nothing is said about longer words. The fuller modern Iban statements conflict: Richards 1981 (pp. xiv-xv) gives penultimate stress unless the penult vowel is e/schwa (then final), unaffected by affixation; Asmah Haji Omar 1969/1981 (section 2.6, the catalog's iban1264 source) gives final stress, non-phonemic, as an intonation element; Scott 1957 (Second Division speakers) reports slightly increased stress on the final syllable in isolation forms. No source describes Balau speech separately.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by Howell & Bailey; Richards 1981 mentions only 'even' stress on penult and final in closed-final words with a penultimate e; StressTyp2 (from Asmah 1981) records no secondary stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Howell & Bailey: only the hedge 'generally'. Richards 1981: penultimate e (schwa) shifts stress to the final; written-but-unpronounced e after r (ter-e-bai = TER-bai); eN+C penults keep stress (EM-pa', REN-tap); pengap invocation recital has 'greatly varied' stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Howell & Bailey speak of the word ('Dyak words... the accented syllable'); Scott 1957 explicitly describes citation forms in isolation (slight final prominence); Asmah 1969 treats stress as a non-phonemic intonation element assigned to emphasised words (the catalog classes iban1264 as LUMPED word/phrase). The statement applies to Iban as a whole; Balau is covered only as one of the tribes within the dictionary's stated scope.
new_statements.identity_note: bala1306 'Balau' is a Glottolog Bookkeeping entry: ISO 639-3 [blg] was retired by Change Request 2020-042 (Anderbeck & Anonby) and merged into Iban [iba] (iban1264): "Balau seemingly was never a distinct language, but rather a somewhat-central Sarawak Iban dialect... Lexical and phonological tests place it within the Iban mainstream." Balau = the Iban of the lower Batang Lupar / Lingga (Banting) area, Second (Sri Aman) Division, Sarawak. No description of Balau speech as such exists; every stress statement found is for Sea Dayak / Iban as a whole (iban1264), whose Second-Division base includes the Balau area. Iban is already in the catalog (unit 133, source of record Asmah Haji Omar 1969 section 2.6 pp. 69-70, final stress, non-phonemic). Cataloguing bala1306 separately would double-count Iban under a retired code, hence candidate_for_catalog = false even though a first-hand statement covering Balau was quoted from a saved file.

sources.note: Iban generally (no dialect singled out): 'the general rule is that [stress falls on the pe]nultimate syllable, unless the vowel is e' (then final); affixation and nasal substitution do not affect the rule; exceptions where a penultimate e syllable is stressed (TER-bai, KER-ja, EM-pa', REN-tap) or stress is even on penult and final when the final is closed; stress 'greatly varied' only in pengap invocation recital.
